When you turn the key in the ignition,
it completes a circuit to the battery,
which sends a burst of electricity to the starter motor.
The starter spins the flywheel, turning the crankshaft and moving the pistons up and down.
As they move, fuel injectors spray gasoline into the cylinders.
igniting the fuel in a small, controlled explosion.
That blast shoves the piston down, and the engine keeps spinning on its own.
The starter lets go, and the car is running.
